nodes.name: Player motor and ground state
nodes.purpose: Fixed-step character controller loop that classifies ground contact, defers to climbing and levitation, and pushes the final displacement through the collider once per physics step.

nodes.name: Classic unit scale and physics step
nodes.purpose: Classic-unit to world-metre scale and the 0.02 second fixed step that every per-tick value in this map is quoted against.

nodes.name: Walking, running and riding speed model
nodes.purpose: Derives ground speed from the Live Speed stat and applies run, sneak, crouch, ride, swim and climb multipliers before the motor consumes it.

nodes.name: Jump, gravity, air control and fall damage
nodes.purpose: Owns the vertical component of player motion: launch impulse, gravity accumulation, ceiling reversal, air steering and the fall-height bookkeeping behind landing damage.

nodes.name: Ground contact and slope sliding
nodes.purpose: Steers the capsule down surfaces steeper than the slope limit, resolves step lips and carries the player along moving platforms.

nodes.name: Capsule height states
nodes.purpose: Blends controller and eye height between standing, crouching, mounted and swimming states without letting the camera enter geometry.

nodes.name: Wall climbing and slipping
nodes.purpose: Attaches the player to vertical surfaces, runs periodic skill checks, wraps strafing around corners and drops the player when a check fails.

nodes.name: Levitation and swimming movement
nodes.purpose: Replacement motor for levitation and swimming: six-direction movement at a fixed levitate speed, or swim speed with a buoyancy ceiling at the water plane.

nodes.name: First-person look, head bob and damage sway
nodes.purpose: Mouse look with pitch clamping and smoothing, velocity-driven head bob amplitudes, and a sine sway triggered by health loss.

nodes.name: Melee swing input and hit detection
nodes.purpose: Turns tracked mouse travel into one of eight swing directions, plays the first-person weapon animation, and resolves reach and line of sight before asking for damage.

nodes.name: Attack resolution formulas
nodes.purpose: Chance to hit, swing modifiers, struck body part selection, weapon and hand-to-hand damage, and backstab multiplication.

nodes.name: Spell and arrow projectiles
nodes.purpose: Fixed-step projectile travel with sphere-cast lookahead, impact payload, by-touch targeting and area explosions.

nodes.name: Enemy senses, pursuit and attacks
nodes.purpose: Sight cone and hearing checks, pursuit that keeps distance from the target, and melee or ranged attack cadence.

nodes.name: Floating origin rebasing
nodes.purpose: Keeps world coordinates near the origin by shifting the player, streamed terrain and loaded enemies whenever the player drifts past a vertical threshold or crosses a map pixel.

cards.name: Ground speed from Live Speed with walk, run, crouch and ride tiers
cards.summary: Ground speed in world units per second is the Live Speed stat plus a stance base, divided by 39.5. Running replaces the walk drag with a skill multiplier.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The motor recomputes speed every 50 Hz fixed step. Walking is (Speed + 150 - drag) / 39.5, where drag is half the gap between 100 and the Speed stat, with the stat floored at 30 inside the drag term only. A Speed stat of 50 therefore walks at about 4.4 units per second. Running drops the drag term and multiplies by 1.35 plus Running skill over 200, so 100 Running gives 1.85. Crouching uses a base of 50 instead of 150 and has no drag. Riding a horse uses a base of 150 + 225 and a cart uses 150 + 100. Riders cannot run. Effect modifiers multiply the result in sequence when the override flag is on, and the product is cached until the base speed changes.

constants.name: classic to world speed ratio
constants.unit: classic speed units per world unit per second; divisor, not a rate

constants.name: walk base
constants.unit: classic speed units added to the Speed stat before the divide; speed recomputed each 50 Hz fixed step

constants.name: crouch base
constants.unit: classic speed units added to the Speed stat before the divide; replaces the walk base

constants.name: ride base bonus
constants.unit: classic speed units added to the walk base while on a horse

constants.name: cart base bonus
constants.unit: classic speed units added to the walk base while in a cart

constants.name: walk drag coefficient
constants.unit: classic speed units removed per point of Speed below 100

constants.name: drag Speed floor
constants.unit: Speed stat points; lower values count as this value in the drag term only

constants.name: run multiplier base
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on the drag-free speed

constants.name: running skill divisor
constants.unit: skill points per 1.0 of extra run multiplier

cards.name: Sneaking halves speed then shaves one classic unit
cards.summary: Sneaking halves the speed built for the current stance and then subtracts one classic speed unit, converted to world units.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The run and sneak state updates only while the player is grounded, and sneak is off whenever run is on. Starting a run clears sneak mode. Sneak takes the speed already built for the stance, divides it by two and subtracts 1 / 39.5, about 0.025 world units per second. Because the second term is fixed, slow characters lose a slightly larger share. While airborne the run state stays as it was, except that it is forced off when the character cannot run, which is the case on a horse or cart. A mounted player takes the ride speed after this step, so sneak has no effect on a mount.

constants.name: sneak speed divisor
constants.unit: divisor on the current ground speed in world units per second

constants.name: sneak flat penalty
constants.unit: classic speed units (1 / 39.5 world units per second) subtracted after halving

cards.name: Jump impulse scaled by skill, athletics and crouch
cards.summary: A jump sets the vertical velocity to 4.5 units per second times a skill, perk and spell multiplier. A 0.1 second grounded gate stops bunny hops.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Jump input is read only on a fixed step where the player is grounded. It is ignored when the player is paralyzed, swimming in exterior water, slow falling or in a cart. It is also ignored until the player has been grounded for 0.1 seconds, unless the player just left a climb. The vertical velocity becomes 4.5 times a multiplier. The multiplier starts at 1, adds Jumping skill times 0.5 over 100, adds 0.1 for Athleticism, 0.1 more for Improved Athleticism and 0.6 under a jump spell. A horse uses a flat 1.75. With gravity 20 the apex is about 0.5 units at skill 0 and about 1.1 units at skill 100. A moving jump adds 0.05 times the base 4.5 along the facing, and a crouched jump scales the vertical velocity by 0.8. The player prefab keeps the 4.5 default.

constants.name: base jump speed
constants.unit: world units per second of vertical launch velocity, applied once per jump; player prefab keeps this value

constants.name: jump skill coefficient
constants.unit: percent of launch speed per point of Jumping skill, applied once per jump

constants.name: athleticism bonus
constants.unit: fraction of launch speed added, applied once per jump

constants.name: improved athleticism bonus
constants.unit: fraction of launch speed added on top of Athleticism, once per jump

constants.name: jump spell bonus
constants.unit: fraction of launch speed added, once per jump

constants.name: crouch jump scale
constants.unit: multiplier on the vertical launch velocity, once per jump

constants.name: grounded time gate
constants.unit: seconds of continuous ground contact required before a jump

constants.name: mounted jump multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on launch speed while riding a horse, once per jump

constants.name: moving jump forward boost
constants.unit: fraction of the base jump speed added along facing, once per jump

cards.name: Gravity accumulation, step anti-bump and slow fall
cards.summary: Vertical velocity loses 20 units per second squared each 50 Hz step. A steady downward push keeps the capsule on stairs, and slow fall is only about 2.1 units per second.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Each fixed step the vertical velocity drops by gravity 20 times the step of 0.02 seconds, and the controller moves by velocity times the step. A step probe casts a 0.1 radius sphere downward from 0.1 units ahead of the capsule centre. When its hit distance lies between half the capsule height minus 0.15 and that plus 1.10, the velocity also drops by 20.75 for that step. While grounded the movement vector is rebuilt each step, so this acts as a steady push of about 21 units per second that keeps the capsule on stairs and ramps. It is skipped while jumping or climbing. Slow fall sets the vertical velocity to minus 105 times the step, which is only about 2.1 units per second at 50 Hz, and it resets the fall origin every step.

constants.name: gravity
constants.unit: world units per second squared, integrated each 50 Hz fixed step; player prefab keeps this value

constants.name: fixed step
constants.unit: seconds per physics step

constants.name: slow fall factor
constants.unit: multiplied by the 0.02 second step to give about 2.1 world units per second downward

constants.name: anti-bump push
constants.unit: world units per second removed from the vertical velocity once per fixed step while the probe band holds

constants.name: step probe inner margin
constants.unit: world units subtracted from half the capsule height to start the probe band

constants.name: step probe band width
constants.unit: world units added to the inner probe range

cards.name: Fall damage threshold and hard landing
cards.summary: A fall of more than 5 units costs 5 health per unit beyond 5. A fall of more than 2.5 units only plays a hard landing sound.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Any step that begins without ground contact records the current height as the fall origin, including the start of a jump. The origin is shifted when the floating origin moves, and it is reset every step during slow fall. On landing the drop is measured from that origin. The check is skipped when the landing tile is exterior water. It is also skipped while climbing, unless the climber is slipping. A drop above 5 units sends a damage message, and the health component removes 5 times the distance beyond 5, rounded down. A drop above 2.5 units sends only a hard landing sound message and no damage. A 7 unit drop therefore costs 10 health.

constants.name: fall damage threshold
constants.unit: world units of drop before damage

constants.name: hard fall divisor
constants.unit: divisor on the threshold for the sound-only hard landing

constants.name: health per unit fallen
constants.unit: health points per world unit beyond the threshold, applied once per landing

cards.name: Air control steering and ceiling reversal
cards.summary: Air steering is off in the shipped player prefab. It turns on only for a jump spell or rappelling. Diagonal input is scaled by 0.7071, and a ceiling hit flips upward velocity.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. While airborne the horizontal velocity is rebuilt from the two movement axes times the current ground speed and rotated into world space. The vertical component is left alone. This runs only when the air control flag, rappelling or a jump spell is active and the player is still in control. The player prefab sets the flag to off, so a normal jump keeps the momentum from takeoff. When both axes are pressed and the diagonal limit is on, which is the default, each axis is scaled by 0.7071. A paralyzed player loses all input. If the capsule reports a hit above while moving up, the vertical velocity is negated at once.

constants.name: air control default
constants.unit: flag; 0 means off in the player prefab

cards.name: Slope limit, step offset and optional slope slide
cards.summary: The player capsule climbs steps up to 0.5 units and slopes up to 70 degrees. An optional slope slide exists but is off in the shipped prefab.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The capsule is a Unity character controller with radius 0.35, a slope limit of 70 degrees, a step offset of 0.5 and a skin width of 0.06. Those values decide which steps and ramps the player walks over. The slide code is a separate option. When enabled it casts down from the capsule centre, falls back to the last contact point, and slides if the surface angle exceeds the slope limit minus 0.1 degrees. The movement vector then points down the slope at 12 units per second and player control is off for that step. The player prefab sets the slide flag and the tagged-surface flag to off, so this slide is inactive by default. Otherwise the input axes are rotated into world space and scaled by ground speed. The move call multiplies the vector by the step, after carrying the player with any moving platform.

constants.name: capsule radius
constants.unit: world units, half extent

constants.name: slope limit
constants.unit: degrees; steeper surfaces block walking

constants.name: step offset
constants.unit: world units of step height the controller climbs

constants.name: slide enabled flag
constants.unit: flag; 0 means the slope slide is off in the player prefab

constants.name: slide speed
constants.unit: world units per second down the slope, only when the slide is enabled; applied each 50 Hz fixed step

cards.name: Capsule and eye height per stance
cards.summary: Standing, crouching, mounted and swimming each have a fixed capsule height, and camera height is half of it minus a small eye offset, blended over a per-stance timer.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The capsule is 1.8 units tall standing, 0.9 crouching, 2.6 mounted and 0.3 swimming. A mounted swimmer is 0.6. Camera height is half the capsule height minus 0.09, so 0.81 standing and 0.36 crouching above the capsule centre. Blend time depends on the action. Crouch, stand and dismount take 0.1 seconds. Mount, forced stand while climbing and the swim crouch take 0.25 seconds. Entering or leaving exterior water takes 0.4 seconds. Crouching lerps the camera down first and shrinks the capsule when the timer ends. Standing grows the capsule at once and lerps the camera up. Standing is blocked while an upward sphere cast of 0.45 units, half the height difference, hits a ceiling.

constants.name: standing capsule height
constants.unit: world units

constants.name: crouch capsule height
constants.unit: world units

constants.name: mounted capsule height
constants.unit: world units

constants.name: swimming capsule height
constants.unit: world units

constants.name: eye offset
constants.unit: world units below the top of the capsule

constants.name: fast blend timer
constants.unit: seconds; crouch, stand and dismount

constants.name: medium blend timer
constants.unit: seconds; mount, climb stand and swim crouch

constants.name: slow blend timer
constants.unit: seconds; entering or leaving exterior water

cards.name: Wall climbing with periodic skill checks
cards.summary: Holding forward against a wall starts a climb after a 14 tick delay. Hold checks every 15 ticks can make the climber slip and fall. The chance comes from the Climbing skill and Luck.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Climbing is allowed only on foot. The player must hold forward, touch a wall and move less than 0.12 units horizontally for a start delay of 14 classic ticks, about 0.77 seconds. A tick is 0.0549 seconds. A grounded start rolls at a 70 percent base, and a roll that fails is retried on later steps, so a grounded start nearly always succeeds. A falling grab rolls at a 40 percent base and resets the delay on a failed roll. The looser 0.9 and 2.0 tolerances and the 5 or 0 tick delays exist only when the Advanced Climbing option is on, which is off by default. Once attached, a hold check runs every 15 ticks, about 0.82 seconds, at a 50 percent base, but only while a move key is down. A failed check makes the climber slip, which counts as falling. A slipping climber is rechecked every 5 ticks at a 20 percent base and takes fall damage when the ground is reached. The chance is the base blended towards 100 by skill, plus up to 10 from Luck. Skill gets 30 more for Khajiit, doubles under a climbing effect, and clamps to 5 through 95 before the blend. Climb speed is ground speed over 3, doubled by the effect.

constants.name: start climb minimum chance
constants.unit: percent per start roll on the ground

constants.name: airborne grasp minimum chance
constants.unit: percent per start roll while falling, once per start delay

constants.name: continue climb minimum chance
constants.unit: percent per hold check

constants.name: regain hold minimum chance
constants.unit: percent per slip recovery check

constants.name: start delay
constants.unit: classic ticks of 0.0549 seconds before the first start roll, with Advanced Climbing off

constants.name: start horizontal tolerance
constants.unit: world units of drift allowed during the start delay, with Advanced Climbing off

constants.name: continue check frequency
constants.unit: classic ticks of 0.0549 seconds per hold check

constants.name: regain check frequency
constants.unit: classic ticks of 0.0549 seconds per slip recovery check

constants.name: climb speed divisor
constants.unit: divisor on ground speed to get climb speed in world units per second

constants.name: climb effect multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on climb speed and on effective skill while a climbing effect is active

constants.name: climbing skill floor
constants.unit: skill points; lower values count as this

constants.name: climbing skill ceiling
constants.unit: skill points; higher values count as this

constants.name: luck bonus maximum
constants.unit: percentage points added to the chance at Luck 100

cards.name: Levitation and swimming movement
cards.summary: While levitating or swimming a replacement motor takes over, moving the player in six directions at a fixed 4 unit levitate speed or at a swim speed derived from the Swimming skill.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. While levitating or swimming the main motor clears its move vector and a separate component moves the player each rendered frame. Horizontal input is rotated by the camera. Vertical input comes from the jump and float up keys for up and the crouch and float down keys for down. Swimming zeroes the vertical part of horizontal input and blocks upward input that would lift the capsule above the water surface, which avoids a pull-back jitter. Levitation uses a flat 4 units per second in every direction. Swimming speed is the base ground speed times Swimming skill over 200, plus a quarter of the base speed. That is 0.25 times walk speed at skill 0 and 0.75 times at skill 100. With water walking active the player moves at normal ground speed. A swimmer sinks when carried weight times 4 exceeds 250, unless levitating, climbing or water walking.

constants.name: levitate move speed
constants.unit: world units per second in any direction, integrated each rendered frame

constants.name: encumbrance multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on carried weight before the sink test

constants.name: encumbrance threshold
constants.unit: weighted units; above this a swimmer sinks

constants.name: swim skill divisor
constants.unit: skill points per 1.0 of swim speed fraction

constants.name: swim flat fraction divisor
constants.unit: divisor on base speed for the flat swim part

cards.name: Mouse look with pitch clamp and smoothing
cards.summary: Look angles accumulate scaled mouse deltas, wrap yaw at 360 degrees, clamp pitch to straight up and down, and chase the target through a frame-rate corrected smoothing weight.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Each rendered frame the raw look delta is multiplied by the sensitivity, which defaults to 2. Controller input is also scaled by 60 times the unscaled frame time, so stick speed does not depend on frame rate. Mouse deltas are not time scaled. Target yaw wraps into 0 to 360. Target pitch clamps to plus or minus 90 degrees by default. The visible angle then moves towards the target as a weighted average. The retained weight is the smoothing setting, 0.5 by default and capped at 0.9, with a 0.5 minimum for a controller. The progress fraction of 1 minus that weight is rescaled from a 60 Hz baseline, so the feel matches at any frame rate.

constants.name: pitch maximum
constants.unit: degrees above the horizon

constants.name: pitch minimum
constants.unit: degrees below the horizon

constants.name: maximum smoothing
constants.unit: upper cap on the retained fraction of the look gap per 60 Hz frame

constants.name: default smoothing
constants.unit: retained fraction of the look gap per 60 Hz frame, from the default settings file

constants.name: default sensitivity
constants.unit: degrees per unit of look delta, mouse and stick scaled differently

constants.name: yaw wrap range
constants.unit: degrees before accumulated yaw is reduced back into range

constants.name: frame rate baseline
constants.unit: frames per second used to rescale smoothing and stick speed

cards.name: Velocity-driven head bob
cards.summary: Camera bob follows horizontal speed. Lateral sway is a cosine and vertical bounce is an absolute sine, with different sizes for walking, running, crouching and riding.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Bob is skipped when the option is off, the player is dead, the cursor is active, the game is paused, the player is climbing or the player is not grounded. Swimming uses zero amplitude. The style is chosen in this order: swimming, running, crouching, riding, walking. Lateral offset is cosine of the phase times the lateral size. Vertical offset is the absolute sine of the phase times the vertical size, so there are two hops per cycle. Walking uses 0.045 lateral and 0.062 vertical, running 0.09 and 0.11, crouching 0.08 and 0.07, riding 0.03 and 0.115. The camera also nods by a small rotation. The phase advances by horizontal speed times 1.25 times the frame time, where 1.25 is half the walk step interval of 2.5, even when running. The start is eased over the first half cycle and the stop is eased over 0.5 seconds. Landing adds a dip of 0.17 units over 0.1 seconds.

constants.name: walking lateral bob
constants.unit: world units of camera offset at full amplitude, each rendered frame

constants.name: walking vertical bob
constants.unit: world units of camera offset at full amplitude, each rendered frame

constants.name: running lateral bob
constants.unit: world units of camera offset at full amplitude, each rendered frame

constants.name: running vertical bob
constants.unit: world units of camera offset at full amplitude, each rendered frame

constants.name: walk step interval
constants.unit: phase units per world unit travelled before halving; same value in the player prefab

constants.name: bob rate divisor
constants.unit: divisor on the walk step interval to get the bob rate

constants.name: stop ease time
constants.unit: seconds to return to the rest position after the player stops

constants.name: landing dip
constants.unit: world units of vertical camera dip over 0.1 seconds after landing

cards.name: Damage camera sway
cards.summary: A health loss above 2 percent of maximum rotates the camera along a random axis. The swing lasts 2.5 to 5 seconds and shrinks as it ends.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The component watches health and ignores a loss of 2 percent of maximum or less. A larger loss starts a sway along a random unit axis made of the pitch and yaw rotation. The phase budget is pi times 5, plus pi for every 20 percent of health lost, rounded down. The phase runs down at 2 pi per second, so a small loss lasts 2.5 seconds and a near fatal loss lasts 5. Each rendered frame the camera is rotated by an extra amount equal to sine of the remaining phase times an amplitude. The amplitude is 50 degrees times the strength setting, times the remaining fraction of the phase, times 0.015 per health point lost clamped to 1. The strength setting scales by 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1, and the default is 3, which is 0.75. The rotation is added per frame and is not corrected for frame rate.

constants.name: maximum recoil severity
constants.unit: degrees of rotation factor before the strength setting

constants.name: default strength setting
constants.unit: setting index; maps to 0.75 of the severity

constants.name: minimum health loss fraction
constants.unit: fraction of maximum health; a loss at or below this is ignored

constants.name: recoil timer speed
constants.unit: multiples of pi per second of sway phase

constants.name: recoil phase base
constants.unit: multiples of pi in the smallest sway phase budget

constants.name: health loss factor
constants.unit: fraction of full amplitude per health point lost, clamped to 1

cards.name: Gesture-driven melee swings
cards.summary: Mouse travel over the last second becomes one of six swing directions once it passes 5 percent of the screen. The hit test at animation frame 2 uses a 2.5 unit reach.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Mouse deltas are summed in a buffer that drops samples older than 1 second. When the path length divided by the longest screen side passes 0.05, the summed vector gives an angle that is bucketed in 15 degree sectors. Right covers 345 to 15 degrees, up covers 15 to 165, left 165 to 195, down-left 195 to 255, down 255 to 285 and down-right 285 to 345. There is no up-left or up-right swing, so up is the widest sector. A stick swings once and re-arms after it returns inside a 0.4 radius. The direction sets the weapon animation, and damage is tested at animation frame 2 for melee or 5 for a bow. The reach is 2.25 plus a 0.25 probe radius. A target needs its centre inside the camera view and a ray of that length from the camera must hit it first. Four extra probes at the head, feet and flanks are used only when the melee detection setting is above 0, and the default is 0.

constants.name: attack travel threshold
constants.unit: fraction of the longest screen side of mouse travel

constants.name: gesture sample window
constants.unit: seconds a mouse sample stays in the gesture buffer

constants.name: swing sector width
constants.unit: degrees per gesture sector

constants.name: stick re-arm radius
constants.unit: stick axis units inside which a stick swing re-arms

constants.name: weapon reach
constants.unit: world units of melee reach before the probe radius; set on the screen weapon, overriding the 2.5 field default

constants.name: melee probe radius
constants.unit: world units added to the reach

constants.name: melee hit frame
constants.unit: animation frame index at which melee damage resolves

constants.name: bow hit frame
constants.unit: animation frame index at which a bow shot resolves

cards.name: Chance to hit with swing trade-offs
cards.summary: Hit chance is the weapon skill plus modifiers for armour, stats, dodge and swing direction, clamped to a 3 to 97 percent band and rolled against a hundred-sided die.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. An attack starts from the attacker live skill for the weapon type, or hand to hand when unarmed. For a player attack the swing direction then changes accuracy and damage. An upward swing adds 10 to hit and takes 4 off damage. A down-right swing adds 5 and takes 2. A down-left swing takes 5 off hit and adds 2 damage. A straight down swing takes 10 off hit and adds 4 damage. Proficiency, racial and backstab modifiers also apply to player attacks only. Armor on the struck body part, adrenaline, enchantments, stat and skill differences and career adjustments are added before the total is clamped to 3 through 97 percent. A d100 roll passes when it is below the chance. The body part comes from a 20 entry table: head 2, each arm 3, chest 4, hands 4, legs 3 and feet 1.

constants.name: minimum hit chance
constants.unit: percent, floor after every modifier

constants.name: maximum hit chance
constants.unit: percent, ceiling after every modifier

constants.name: upward swing accuracy
constants.unit: percentage points of hit chance

constants.name: down-right swing damage
constants.unit: damage points

constants.name: down-right swing accuracy
constants.unit: percentage points of hit chance

constants.name: down-left swing damage
constants.unit: damage points

constants.name: down-left swing accuracy
constants.unit: percentage points of hit chance

constants.name: downward swing damage

cards.name: Weapon and hand-to-hand damage
cards.summary: Damage rolls inside the weapon's own range, then adds swing, proficiency, racial, strength and material modifiers, with a separate curve for unarmed strikes.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. A weapon is checked first against the target minimum metal, and a weaker material does zero damage. A hit rolls uniformly between the weapon base minimum and maximum and adds the swing, proficiency and racial modifiers. A skeletal warrior then halves that sum for a weapon without the edged flag and doubles it for silver. Strength adds a table modifier and the weapon material adds a second modifier, which is half of what the inventory screen suggests. A total below 1 becomes 0, and then the career bonus or penalty for the enemy type is added. Unarmed strikes roll between one tenth of the hand to hand skill plus 1 and one fifth of the skill plus 1. They add the same modifiers and add the strength bonus for the player only. A career bonus or phobia adds or subtracts the attacker level against humans, undead, daedra or animals.

constants.name: hand to hand minimum divisor
constants.unit: skill points per point of minimum unarmed damage

constants.name: hand to hand minimum offset
constants.unit: damage points added to the minimum unarmed roll

constants.name: hand to hand maximum divisor
constants.unit: skill points per point of maximum unarmed damage

constants.name: skeletal non-edged divisor
constants.unit: divisor on damage from weapons without the edged flag

constants.name: skeletal silver multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on damage from silver weapons

cards.name: Backstab bonus from behind
cards.summary: A player attack on a back-facing enemy adds the Backstabbing skill to hit chance and triples damage on a percentile roll.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The player melee path marks a swing as a backstab when the enemy sprite is back-facing and is not mid way through a transformation. For player attacks, the live Backstabbing skill is then added to the hit chance, and the skill gains one use. After a hit, damage is tripled when the skill is above 1 and a d100 roll falls below the skill. The skill is therefore both the accuracy bonus and the triple damage chance in percent. At skill 50 that is a 50 percent chance of triple damage. Enemy attacks never backstab.

constants.name: backstab damage multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on damage after a successful roll

constants.name: backstab minimum skill
constants.unit: skill points; the triple roll runs only above this value

cards.name: Projectile travel and area impact
cards.summary: Missiles move at 25 units per second. Hits are tested with a 0.45 unit sphere cast each 50 Hz step. Area spells burst in a 4 unit radius.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. The visible missile moves along its aim direction each rendered frame at 25 units per second. Hit testing runs on each 50 Hz fixed step as a cast of 0.5 units, the step distance, plus the 0.45 radius. The first step uses a ray, because the caster may touch a wall. Later steps use a sphere cast, so fast missiles do not tunnel through thin geometry. A hit on an entity applies the payload to it. Only an area-at-range spell then gathers every entity inside 4 units of the impact point. An area-around-caster spell does the same around the caster and skips the caster. The player aims along the camera forward. An enemy aims at the predicted target position when enhanced combat AI is on, which is the default, otherwise at the last known position. A missile expires 8 seconds after release if nothing is hit. The light turns off 0.6 seconds after impact, and the object is removed once its impact sound ends. A touch spell sphere casts 3 units with a 0.25 radius. The 0.9 unit arm length is used only by the enemy check for a clear shot.

cards.name: Enemy sight cone, hearing and target prediction
cards.summary: Enemies see about 102 units inside a 190 degree cone and need a clear line. They hear 25 units unless static geometry is in the way.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Sight range is 4096 classic units times 0.025, which is 102.4 units, plus a per-enemy sight modifier. The target must be inside half the field of view of the enemy facing. That field is 180 degrees in the classic setting and 190 when enhanced combat AI is on, which is the default. A ray from eye height to the target eye height must also hit the target first. Hearing is a radius of 25 units plus a per-enemy modifier, and it fails when a static geometry hit lies between them. Doors and other moving objects do not block hearing. With enhanced AI, target prediction runs when 0.0625 seconds have passed, which is every fourth 50 Hz step or 0.08 seconds. It solves a quadratic for the earliest intercept point, using the target velocity and an intercept speed of the enemy walk speed or the missile speed.

cards.name: Enemy melee and ranged attack cadence
cards.summary: Enemies swing after a cooldown of about 1.5 to 3.1 seconds, shortened by player level and lengthened by slower reflexes. They need 22.5 degrees of facing and 2.25 units of reach.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. A melee attempt starts on a classic update tick when the cooldown is zero and a random check on the enemy speed passes. A faster enemy passes more often. The target must be in sight within 22.5 degrees of facing, and within 2.25 units plus the rate at which the target is closing. The 1.5 unit distance against other AI applies only when enhanced combat AI is off, and it is on by default. The damage frame has its own test: distance at most 0.25, or at most 2.25 and within 35.156 degrees of facing. Each attack rolls a cooldown of 1500 to 3000 classic frames. It subtracts 50 for each player level above 10, adds 450 for each reflexes step below Average, then divides by 980 to get seconds. At level 10 and Average reflexes that is 1.5 to 3.1 seconds. Ranged attacks start between 6 and 51.2 units. With enhanced AI the enemy halves its move speed while an attack animation plays.

cards.name: Floating origin rebasing for a continent-scale world
cards.summary: The player and the streamed world are shifted when the height passes 500 units either way or the map pixel changes, which keeps float coordinates small.
cards.behavior: Reimplementation note: this repository is a Unity reimplementation of the classic game, and values below are from that reimplementation. Each 50 Hz fixed step the origin keeper compares the player height against a limit of 500 units above or below zero. It also compares the current map pixel with the last one. A height breach shifts everything by the negated height. A pixel change shifts by the pixel delta times the terrain tile size scaled to world units. When anything changed, the player controller, the streamed terrain children and the active enemies take the same offset in one step. The player fall origin is adjusted in the same pass, so the shift is not read as a fall. This is an engine precision technique, and it is useful only for a very large outdoor map.

constants.name: vertical rebase threshold
constants.unit: world units of height drift, above or below zero, before the origin is shifted
